title: HR Policy 6009 - TB Screening
chunks: ST. MARY'S HOME HUMAN RESOURCES Employment Regulation Cross Reference: Policy # 6009 Page 1 of 2 Licensing: 12 VAC 35-46-250, 300 Licensing: 12VAC 35-105-510 Subject: TUBERCULOSIS SCREENING Dum 3 lan a Issued: May 2025 Revised: 7/2025, 8/2025, 2/2026 PURPOSE: The purpose of this policy is to ensure the health and safety of all individuals working with individuals who live at St. Mary's Home by preventing the transmission of tuberculosis (TB). This policy outlines the required screening procedures for employees, contractors, SECEP staff, students, and volunteers to identify and manage TB risk in compliance with applicable public health guidelines and infection control standards. PROCEDURE: New Employees Contractors, Volunteers, Students, and SECEP staff 1. Mandatory Tuberculosis Screening is required. No individual will be allowed to start working or participate in orientation until a statement of certification by a qualified licensed practitioner indicating the absence of tuberculosis ina communicable form as evidenced by the completion of a form containing, at a minimum, the elements of a current screening form published by the Virginia Department of Health. The screening assessment shall be no older than 30 days. 2. Asstatement of certification shall not be required for a new employee who has separated from service with another licensed provider with a break in service of six months or less or who is currently working for another licensed provider. A copy of the original screening result must be provided to HR and the SMH Health Compliance Nurse prior to start of orientation. Additional screening/testing may be required at the discretion of the Health Compliance Nurse. 3. Contractors, Volunteers, students, and SECEP staff will provide negative TB test results or will have their TB screening done by the SMH Health Compliance Nurse Prior to direct contact with individuals receiving services. 4. On the first day of new employee orientation, all new employees will be given a PPD by the SMH Health Compliance Nurse or Designee. The PPD will be read in 48-72 hours. If the PPD is not read within this time frame, the PPD will need to be repeated. 5. If the PPD result is positive, the employee will be referred to Occupational Health for follow up testing. A staff with a positive PPD result will not be allowed to continue in orientation until cleared by Occupational Health. 6. A negative QuantiFERON test (QFT) obtained 30 days prior to hire is an acceptable substitute for PPD. Current Employees, Contractors, Volunteers, Students and SECEP staff 1. Annual Tuberculosis Screening via questionnaire and tuberculosis education are a mandatory requirement for continued employment and contact with individuals receiving services. 2. Additional TB screening such as TST/PPD, blood test, and/or chest x-ray may be required as deemed necessary by the SMH Health Compliance Nurse. 3. Any employee, contractor, student, or volunteer employee who recently traveled to Africa, Asia, Mexico, Central & South America, The Caribbean, and Eastem Europe should report to the Health Compliance Nurse for Tuberculosis Screening upon return to work. 4. Any employee, contractor, student, or volunteer employee who recently traveled to Africa, Asia, Mexico, Central & South America, The Caribbean, and Eastem Europe should report to the Health Compliance Nurse for Tuberculosis Screening upon return to work. 4. Any employee, contractor, student, or volunteer who has a known exposure to tuberculosis should report to the SMH Health Compliance Nurse for TB screening. 5. Any employee, contractor, student, or volunteer who comes in contact with a known case of active tuberculosis disease or who develops symptoms of active tuberculosis disease (including, but not limited to fever, chills, hemoptysis, cough, fatigue, night sweats, weight loss , or anorexia) of three weeks duration shall be screened as determined appropriate for continued contact with employees, contractors, students, volunteers, or individuals receiving services based on consuitation with the local health department. 6. Any employee, contractor, student, or volunteer suspected of having active tuberculosis shall not be permitted to retum to work or have contact with employees, contractors, students, volunteers or individuals receiving services until a physician has determined that the person is free of active tuberculosis. 2|Page
